verifiedAgainst: @dabowman/archer: src/components/index.ts (the package's export list, 56 component folders) and each component's own source, read 2026-09-14
note: Component currency, not props. Archer is one package on one release line, so nothing here is `legacy` or `locked` yet — the registry exists so that the day something is deprecated, `system/superseded-component` has somewhere to say so, and so `loupe-authoring` has a single answer to 'which component is this'. Entries are the roots a consumer chooses *between*. Every root ships flat part exports off the same import (`Dialog`, `DialogTrigger`, `DialogPopup`, … — not `Dialog.Root`), and the parts are that root's anatomy rather than a separate choice, so they are not listed one by one; the `note` on a root names the parts where the wrong one is actually reachable. Archer wraps Base UI for behaviour and supplies its own styling, so a part's props are Base UI's props plus Archer's `variant`/`size` where the root declares them — read the component's own `.tsx` or its Storybook page for those. Re-verify against `src/components/` before bumping this file's version.

components.name: Stack
components.note: Layout primitive for siblings along one axis. Base UI ships no layout, so flow and spacing are Archer's half of the job: `direction`, `gap` (single space steps `4xs`…`3xl`), `align`, `justify`, `wrap`. Anything spacing siblings is this, not a margin. Cells that must line up in columns across rows are `Grid`, not a wrapping `Stack`.

components.name: Grid
components.note: Layout primitive for cells in columns — a row of cards. `min` (a CSS length, default `16rem`) is the narrowest a column may be; `gap` takes the same single space steps as `Stack`. The column count is not a prop: the grid fits as many columns as the container holds, and a short last row keeps the columns above it.

components.name: Center
components.note: Layout primitive that caps a column's width and centres it. `max`: `content` (the default, `--size-content`, a screen's main column) | `measure` (`--size-measure`, prose or a single-column form). A screen caps its column with this rather than a `max-width` of its own.

components.name: AppShell
components.note: The frame of an application: skip link, sticky top bar, navigation column, focusable `main`. Its regions are props, not children — `brand`, `actions`, `nav` (a vertical `NavigationMenu`) — and `children` is the page. It collapses on its own width, opening the same `nav` in a `Drawer`, so do not build a second mobile navigation beside it.

components.name: PageHeader
components.note: The block at the top of a screen or pane — the shared implementation of `screen#header` in the pattern registry. Props: `title`, `level` (default 1; 2 for a pane), `description`, `breadcrumb` (a `Breadcrumb`), `actions`; `children` is the row under the title, for a `TabsList` or a horizontal `NavigationMenu`. The title is already a `Heading` with `variant="ui"`.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.note: The trail above the current page: a named `nav` around an ordered list. Parts: `BreadcrumbItem` (`href`, `current` for the page the user is on, `render` for a router link). The separators are CSS — do not put slashes in the markup.

components.name: Heading
components.note: Every heading. `level` (1–6, default 2) sets the element and the size together. `variant`: `prose` (the default, `heading-1`…`heading-6`) | `ui` (`ui-title` at level 1, `ui-heading` below it) — use `ui` on application screens. Never pick a level for its size.

components.name: Text
components.note: A paragraph of running prose. `variant`: `body-1` | `body-2` (default) | `body-3`. These are the prose type styles; text inside a control is the control's job, not this.

components.name: Link
components.note: An inline link in text, underlined at rest. In a `Menu`, `NavigationMenu`, `Toolbar` or `Breadcrumb`, use that component's own link part instead.

components.name: List
components.note: A bulleted list, or numbered with `ordered`. Parts: `ListItem`. Item spacing is the list's `gap`.

components.name: Code
components.note: Code inline in a sentence, or a `<pre>` block with `block`. No syntax highlighting.

components.name: Quote
components.note: A block quotation, with an optional `attribution`.

components.name: Image
components.note: An image with an optional `caption`. `alt` is required, including `""` for a decorative image.

components.name: Card
components.note: A bordered surface grouping related content. It carries a uniform `gap` between its children, so a child sets no margin. A row of cards is a `Grid` of `Card`s.

components.name: Table
components.note: Tabular data, in a scroll container that becomes a focusable region only while it overflows. `striped`, `scrollLabel`. Parts are plain table elements: `TableCaption`, `TableHead`, `TableBody`, `TableRow`, `TableHeaderCell`, `TableCell`. Never rebuild a table from `Grid` or `Stack`.

components.name: Alert
components.note: A message that stays on the page — a form's error summary, a notice about what is shown. `intent`: info | success | warning | error, which also sets the live-region role. `title`, `icon`. A message that leaves on its own is a toast (`useToastManager`); one that blocks until answered is `AlertDialog`.

components.name: Badge
components.note: A short label: a status, a count, a category. `variant`: neutral | brand | info | success | warning | error. Not a control — a label that filters when clicked is a `Toggle`, one removed from a set is a `ComboboxChip`.

components.name: Empty
components.note: What a list, table or panel shows when it correctly holds nothing — the shared implementation of `report.empty` in the pattern registry. `title`, `description`, `icon`; `children` is the way out, usually one `Button`. Not a failure (`Alert`) and not a wait (`Spinner`, `Skeleton`).

components.name: Spinner
components.note: An indeterminate wait with nothing to measure, sized to a control's icon slot. `label`. A wait with a number is `Progress`.

components.name: Skeleton
components.note: A placeholder for content whose layout is known in advance. `lines`, `circle`. Hidden from assistive technology: put `aria-busy` on the region being filled. If the layout is not known, that is `Spinner`.

components.name: Button
components.note: `variant`: primary | secondary | outline | ghost. `size`: sm | md | lg. Inside a `Toolbar`, use `ToolbarButton` instead — it takes the toolbar's roving-focus wiring, which a bare `Button` does not.

components.name: Toggle
components.note: A pressed/unpressed control (`aria-pressed`). Not a `Switch`, which is an on/off setting, and not a `Checkbox`, which is a form value.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.note: A set of `Toggle`s sharing one value — a segmented control. Base UI's toggle-group props (`value`, `multiple`, …). Choosing one of several views or modes is this, not a row of `Button`s holding pressed state by hand.

components.name: Switch
components.note: An on/off setting that applies immediately. A setting that only applies on submit is a `Checkbox`.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.note: The container; `Radio` is one option and is never used outside it.

components.name: Radio
components.note: One option inside a `RadioGroup`.

components.name: Input
components.note: A bare text input. Wrap it in `Field` when it needs a label, description or error — `Field` owns that rhythm as a gap. Multi-line is `Textarea`.

components.name: Textarea
components.note: A multi-line text field with `Input`'s paint. Composes with `Field` the way `Input` does.

components.name: OTPField
components.note: Parts: `OTPFieldInput`, `OTPFieldSeparator`.

components.name: Field
components.note: The label/control/description/error row. Parts: `FieldLabel`, `FieldControl`, `FieldDescription`, `FieldError`, `FieldValidity`. Reach for this before hand-stacking a label above an input.

components.name: Fieldset
components.note: A group of related fields. Parts: `FieldsetLegend`.

components.name: Slider
components.note: Single value. Two thumbs is `RangeSlider`.

components.name: Select
components.note: Choosing one predefined value — the trigger shows the current value. Parts: `SelectTrigger`, `SelectPopup`, `SelectOption`, `SelectGroup`, `SelectGroupLabel`. For commands or navigation, that is `Menu`; for free-form filtering, `Autocomplete` or `Combobox`.

components.name: Combobox
components.note: A value chosen from a list the user can filter, including multi-select via `ComboboxChips`. Parts: `ComboboxField`, `ComboboxInput`, `ComboboxTrigger`, `ComboboxClear`, `ComboboxValue`, `ComboboxPopup`, `ComboboxList`, `ComboboxItem`, `ComboboxGroup`, `ComboboxGroupLabel`, `ComboboxEmpty`, `ComboboxChips`, `ComboboxChip`, `ComboboxChipRemove`.

components.name: Autocomplete
components.note: Free-form text with suggestions — the typed value is valid even when nothing matches. If the value must come from the list, that is `Combobox`. Parts: `AutocompleteInput`, `AutocompleteClear`, `AutocompletePopup`, `AutocompleteList`, `AutocompleteItem`, `AutocompleteGroup`, `AutocompleteGroupLabel`, `AutocompleteEmpty`.

components.name: Dialog
components.note: A focused task in an overlay. Parts: `DialogTrigger`, `DialogPopup`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription`, `DialogClose`. A destructive confirmation is `AlertDialog`; a longer flow or an edit of something already on screen is `Drawer`.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.note: Destructive or irreversible confirmation — dismissal behaviour and emphasis already match the severity. Parts: `AlertDialogTrigger`, `AlertDialogPopup`, `AlertDialogTitle`, `AlertDialogDescription`, `AlertDialogClose`. Never rebuild this out of `Dialog` + two `Button`s.

components.name: Drawer
components.note: An edge-anchored panel for multi-field or multi-step work a `Dialog` would cramp. Parts: `DrawerTrigger`, `DrawerPopup`, `DrawerTitle`, `DrawerDescription`, `DrawerClose`.

components.name: Popover
components.note: Non-modal, anchored, interactive. Parts: `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverPopup`, `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverDescription`, `PopoverClose`. Text-only on hover is `Tooltip`; a rich hover summary is `PreviewCard`.

components.name: PreviewCard
components.note: A rich hover preview of a link or entity. Parts: `PreviewCardTrigger`, `PreviewCardPopup`.

components.name: Tooltip
components.note: A short text label on hover/focus. It carries no interactive content — if it needs a button, it wanted `Popover`.

components.name: Menu
components.note: Commands, navigation destinations and in-menu settings. Parts: `MenuTrigger`, `MenuPopup`, `MenuItem` (commands), `MenuLinkItem` (navigation), `MenuCheckboxItem`/`MenuRadioGroup`/`MenuRadioItem` (settings), `MenuGroup`, `MenuGroupLabel`, `MenuSeparator`, `MenuSub`, `MenuSubTrigger`, `MenuArrow`, `MenuBackdrop`. Choosing a value is `Select`, not this.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.note: The same menu opened by right-click on a target. Parts: `ContextMenuTrigger`, `ContextMenuPopup`, `ContextMenuItem`, `ContextMenuSeparator`, `ContextMenuGroup`, `ContextMenuGroupLabel`.

components.name: Menubar
components.note: A persistent horizontal bar of menus. Parts: `MenubarItem`.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.note: Site or app navigation with rich panels. Parts: `NavigationMenuList`, `NavigationMenuItem`, `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `NavigationMenuContent`, `NavigationMenuPopup`, `NavigationMenuLink`, `NavigationMenuArrow`.

components.name: Toolbar
components.note: A roving-focus action bar. Parts: `ToolbarGroup`, `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarLink`, `ToolbarInput`, `ToolbarSeparator`. Its children must be the `Toolbar*` parts — a plain `Button` inside a `Toolbar` drops out of the roving-focus order.

components.name: Tabs
components.note: Peer views of one subject, all at the same level. Parts: `TabsList`, `TabsTab`, `TabsPanel`. Tabs standing in for hierarchy is the usual misuse — depth wants navigation, not tabs.

components.name: Accordion
components.note: Several independently expandable sections. Parts: `AccordionItem`, `AccordionHeader`, `AccordionTrigger`, `AccordionPanel`. One section on its own is `Collapsible`.

components.name: Collapsible
components.note: One show/hide region. Parts: `CollapsibleTrigger`, `CollapsiblePanel`.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.note: A scroll container with styled scrollbars. Only where the scrollbar itself has to be styled — ordinary overflow does not need it.

components.name: Separator
components.note: A visible divider. It carries no spacing of its own by default; the surrounding rhythm belongs to the parent's `gap`.

components.name: Progress
components.note: Progress toward completion. A static measurement of a value in a range is `Meter`; a wait with no number is `Spinner`.

components.name: Meter
components.note: A static measurement within a known range (disk used, score). Not progress.

components.name: ToastProvider
components.note: Mount once at the app root. Toasts are then raised from `useToastManager()`, not by rendering a component — a hand-built notification stack is rebuilding what the manager already owns.

components.name: useToastManager
components.note: The hook that raises a toast. Requires `ToastProvider` above it.
